authority: T0 partial evidence-register intake for the common T-053 boundary benchmark; not a charter-complete freeze, TECT claim, candidate selection, physical-vacuum result, or Pre-A exit
scope: A first candidate-neutral boundary intake only: electromagnetic Lorentz anisotropy and dispersion, gravitational-wave/electromagnetic propagation, superconducting flux periodicity and quantization, and controlled critical scaling. Dataset/table locators and uncertainty models are recorded, but the full Pre-A evidence families and common observable map are incomplete.

versioning_policy.admission_rule: Only directly measured observables with primary experimental or official archival provenance enter this tranche. Structural interpretations are deliberately weaker than candidate narratives.

evidence_items.observable: orientation-dependent relative beat-frequency modulation Delta_nu/nu in two orthogonal cryogenic sapphire oscillators

source.title: Direct terrestrial test of Lorentz symmetry in electrodynamics to 10^-18

evidence_items.dataset_or_table: published main-result fit and supplementary harmonic-amplitude tables
evidence_items.uncertainty_model: the reported central value and 95% confidence interval, with material-resonator and magnetic-systematic qualifications retained
evidence_items.independence_rationale: terrestrial rotating-cavity apparatus independent of the astrophysical and condensed-matter anchors; photon and electron SME interpretations are not counted as independent measurements
evidence_items.minimum_constraint: A viable low-energy electromagnetic sector must suppress orientation-dependent propagation or resonator-frequency anisotropy to the measured scale under the declared apparatus and test framework.
evidence_items.systematic_and_model_boundary: The experimental observable is a material-resonator beat frequency. Several reported SME coefficient bounds assume an electron-sector convention or constrain photon-electron combinations; the datum is not a model-free measurement of a standalone microscopic light speed.
does_not_license: equality of every particle or collective-mode speed

evidence_items.observable: arrival-time delay between GRB 170817A and GW170817
evidence_items.reported_value: +1.74 +/- 0.05 s; inferred (v_GW-v_EM)/v_EM in [-3 x 10^-15, +7 x 10^-16] under the collaboration's emission-delay assumptions

source.title: Gravitational Waves and Gamma-rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A
source.authors: LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, Fermi GBM, and INTEGRAL

evidence_items.dataset_or_table: collaboration paper timing result and derived speed-bound section
evidence_items.uncertainty_model: reported detector timing uncertainty plus the collaboration's conservative intrinsic-emission-delay interval; the speed interval is conditional on that source model
evidence_items.independence_rationale: independent gravitational-wave and gamma-ray instruments observe one associated source, so detector independence is retained while source association and emission physics remain shared nuisances
evidence_items.minimum_constraint: A viable shared low-energy causal structure must reproduce the observed near-coincidence of gravitational-wave and electromagnetic propagation after explicitly modelling source-emission delay and propagation effects.
evidence_items.systematic_and_model_boundary: The speed interval uses an assumed range for the intrinsic gamma-ray emission delay and one source association. It compares gravitational and gamma-ray signals, not all matter, gauge, or collective modes.
does_not_license: derivation of the speed of light from a candidate lattice

evidence_items.observable: discrete trapped magnetic-flux states in multiply connected superconducting cylinders or rings
evidence_items.reported_value: independent 1961 experiments found flux steps compatible with a basic unit near hc/(2e); the Doll-Nabauer abstract reports about 40% of hc/e

sources.title: Experimental Evidence for Quantized Flux in Superconducting Cylinders
sources.authors: B. S. Deaver Jr. and W. M. Fairbank

sources.title: Experimental Proof of Magnetic Flux Quantization in a Superconducting Ring
sources.source_type: independent primary experiment archived by OSTI

evidence_items.dataset_or_table: the two 1961 primary reports and their archived abstracts; the present intake does not reconstruct raw magnetometer traces
evidence_items.uncertainty_model: historical apparatus precision and geometry/calibration limitations as reported; no modern combined confidence interval is manufactured
evidence_items.independence_rationale: two independent groups and apparatuses reported the same half-electron-pair flux scale; they share superconducting theory and period-calibration assumptions
evidence_items.minimum_constraint: Controlled condensed-matter systems can realize a coherent compact phase or equivalent winding structure with reproducible discrete flux sectors. Any candidate invoking an analogous mechanism must define its compact variable, charge normalization, and finite-energy winding sectors rather than infer them from a real scalar modulation.
evidence_items.systematic_and_model_boundary: These are historical superconducting-material measurements with their original precision and apparatus assumptions. The compact-phase interpretation uses superconducting theory and does not transfer automatically to empty space.
does_not_license: a universal value of microscopic charge
identification of a mathematical defect with a particle

evidence_items.observable: specific-heat singularity of liquid helium-4 near the lambda transition in microgravity
evidence_items.reported_value: alpha = -0.0127 +/- 0.0003; measurements reached within 2 nK of the transition with no observed rounding at that resolution

source.title: Specific Heat of Liquid Helium in Zero Gravity very near the Lambda Point
source.authors: J. A. Lipa, J. A. Nissen, D. A. Stricker, D. R. Swanson, and T. C. P. Chui

evidence_items.dataset_or_table: published final exponent fit, amplitude-ratio fit, and near-transition residual/rounding analysis
evidence_items.uncertainty_model: reported fit uncertainty with thermometry, background, correction-to-scaling, and fit-window systematics retained as one experiment rather than multiplied
evidence_items.independence_rationale: microgravity helium experiment independent of propagation and superconducting apparatus; alpha and its amplitude ratio share the same data and are one evidence group
evidence_items.minimum_constraint: A candidate that claims a particular universality mechanism must derive its static exponents, scaling window, and finite-size or rounding corrections before comparison; a generic statement that a phase transition occurs is insufficient.
evidence_items.systematic_and_model_boundary: This is a helium-4 material transition and alpha is a specific-heat exponent. Converting it to a correlation-length exponent requires additional scaling assumptions; neither its universality class nor numerical value is evidence for a vacuum transition without a derived observable map.
does_not_license: a TECT critical exponent by analogy

evidence_items.observable: energy-dependent arrival-time dispersion in GRB 090510 over the reported 35 MeV to 31 GeV range
evidence_items.reported_value: |Delta t/Delta E| < 30 ms/GeV at 99% confidence; for the declared linear-dispersion model M_QG,1/M_Planck > 1.22
evidence_items.units: milliseconds per GeV and dimensionless scale ratio

source.title: A limit on the variation of the speed of light arising from quantum gravity effects
source.authors: Fermi LAT and Fermi GBM Collaborations

evidence_items.dataset_or_table: published high-energy photon chronology and 99% confidence dispersion analyses
evidence_items.uncertainty_model: reported photon-energy and timing uncertainties together with alternative intrinsic-source-lag controls; the two analyses of the same burst are not treated as independent replications
evidence_items.independence_rationale: a distinct event from GW170817 but with Fermi instrumentation in both gamma-ray evidence groups, so instrument correlation is explicitly retained
evidence_items.minimum_constraint: A candidate predicting a linear photon dispersion over the tested energy and background range must suppress its coefficient at least to the reported conditional scale or explain why the observable map differs.
evidence_items.systematic_and_model_boundary: The bound assumes a cosmological propagation model and controls rather than eliminates intrinsic source lag. It does not constrain energy-independent shifts or every quadratic and higher-order dispersion law.
does_not_license: a bound on all particle sectors
using the Planck scale as a predicted TECT output

evidence_items.observable: superfluid-density critical exponent of helium-4 near the lambda transition

source.title: The exponent of the superfluid density of He-4 near T_lambda

evidence_items.dataset_or_table: published reanalysis result; original measurement lineage must still be reconstructed before charter-complete evidence freeze
evidence_items.uncertainty_model: reported reanalysis uncertainty; relation to the correlation-length exponent is conditional on an additional Josephson-scaling hypothesis
evidence_items.independence_rationale: different helium response and earlier experimental lineage than the Lipa specific-heat flight, but shared universality assumptions prevent treating the two exponents as model-free independent vacuum evidence
evidence_items.validation_rule: The value is public and therefore not blind or sealed. Do not use it to choose field number, symmetry, kinetic coefficients, or candidate parameters; preregister the mapped stiffness exponent and corrections-to-scaling convention before scoring it.
evidence_items.minimum_constraint: A candidate claiming the same controlled universality mechanism must predict the relevant stiffness or superfluid-density exponent under a declared observable map, not infer it from a fitted alpha.
evidence_items.systematic_and_model_boundary: The result is a reanalysis of helium measurements and is not independent evidence for a vacuum order parameter. Relation to nu uses an additional Josephson-scaling hypothesis.
does_not_license: using zeta as an inserted TECT parameter
identifying zeta with nu without a scaling proof
claiming a shared universality class before the preregistered non-fitting prediction is scored

calibration_authorities.reported_value: 2.067833848... x 10^-15 Wb, exact in the present SI because h and e are defining constants

source.title: SI Brochure, Appendix 2: mise en pratique for the ampere and other electric units

calibration_authorities.boundary: Definitional exactness calibrates units; it is not another experiment and does not derive h or e from a candidate.

no_overclaim: This register records a small candidate-neutral discovery intake and one visible non-fitting validation target. It does not satisfy the charter's complete evidence-freeze condition, show that the listed phenomena share one microscopic cause, show that a vacuum is a superconductor or helium-like medium, show that any candidate passes T-053, select an action, exit Pre-A, or change Sector-A tier or scope.
